scope: Corollary 9.5 (Confined macroscopic-gap arches) of the manuscript “Critical honeycomb chords with prescribed boundary endpoints” (preprints/Critical-honeycomb-chords-with-prescribed-boundary-endpoints-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6b7adfc0aa278ae3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 39. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a half-plane boundary source and choose a sufficiently large fixed C. Give each arch with terminal gap in [h, 2h] on one chosen side and diameter at most Ch its critical weight, then normalize over this entire set of terminal ports. For every integer h → ∞, L(γ) = h4/3+o(1) in probability, EL(γ) = h4/3+o(1) .
